claims.text: Replacing standard EAM reference potentials with a machine-learning interatomic potential will improve coverage of liquid-phase configuration space.
The machine-learning potential will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to EAM references.
The proposed potential is to be trained on ab initio molecular-dynamics data for multicomponent high-entropy alloys at high temperatures.
The target systems contain at least four principal elements and include both solid and liquid states near their melting temperatures.
The target solid and liquid states have random elemental site occupancy.
The applicable temperature range is approximately 0.8–1.0 times the melting temperature.
The method applies to equimolar or near-equimolar alloys containing multiple transition-metal or refractory elements.
A high-fidelity machine-learning potential can accurately capture short- and medium-range coordination motifs in liquid-like and high-temperature solid structures.
Improved representation of a broad range of local bonding environments will make the reference potential more closely reproduce ab initio forces and energies.
Closer reproduction of ab initio forces and energies will reduce discrepancies along the thermodynamic-integration path.
The expected reduction in free-energy path divergence is on the order of tens of meV per atom or better.
Standard EAM potentials are used as references in TOR-TILD.
EAM references exhibit appreciable mismatch for the liquid phase.
High-temperature multicomponent alloys can exhibit chemical clustering and short-range ordering.
Insufficient sampling of configuration space can cause the machine-learning potential to miss ordering or short-range structures.
The intervention is limited to compositions and temperatures for which sufficient, high-quality ab initio training data can be generated.
The hypothesis is falsified if the machine-learning-based free-energy error exceeds 20 meV per atom on average.
Failure to reproduce crucial high-temperature structures observed in ab initio simulations also falsifies the hypothesis.
